message.content:
VOTE: APPROVE

Both Round-4 rejections were resolved by verification, not negotiation. Sol's eligibility rule is now executable, and the check of `frekvensgate_resultat.json` establishes that the m%3==0 thinned set is origin-identical to the 198 quarterly origins (0 label disagreements, same pooled base rate 0.1616). That converts my Round-4 reservation 2 from "close, not exact" to exact, and Grok's objection is answered by artifact, not assertion. All three of my Round-4 reservations are now in the text: nested oracle-free computed at the 2027 refit (§1.2), the paired diagnostic re-run with code-checked origin identity (§3.3), three censoring variants with real-time first (§6.2). Neither veto is triggered.

Reservations for the record (non-blocking):

1. **§3.2(b) — pin the artifact by hash, and record what 0.02 pp means.** With origin identity established, the executed gate failed by 0.02 pp against a paired SD of 2.58 pp — 0.008 SD. The paired difference itself is −0.40 SD with an interval [−4.47, +1.32] that does not favour monthly. The minutes should state this in numbers: the council is not overriding evidence, it is declining to act on noise. And because −1.02 pp is the load-bearing reason for declining a preregistered gate, the JSON's commit hash belongs in the minutes — a path can be regenerated, a hash cannot. The secretary verified its own artifact; independent reproduction is noted, but the pin should be cryptographic.

2. **§3.3 — pin the normalisation numerically, not as a promise.** "Including the loss/penalty normalisation" is not a number. Under a summed loss, λ_m = λ_q·(N_m/N_q) ≈ 3.0; E2's counterfactual monthly fit (β −1.41 vs −1.29; live P 14.4 vs 14.9) ran at roughly one-third effective shrinkage, so the unscored column as prototyped confounds sampling frequency with relaxed penalisation. The sealed spec should state the chosen normalisation and its value before any run.

3. **§9.3 — add 1980–81 to the date-stamped tests.** 1991/2001 exercise the trough-lag term; the double-dip is the hardest case for §9.2 condition (2): E5's 83 open-episode months include the entire 1980-08..1981-05 run-up (10 positive rows, P to 96.6 %). A test suite that skips back-to-back onsets has not tested censoring resolution where it actually binds.

Let me think about what Kimi K3 should do in Round 5.

The Round 4 draft got 5 APPROVE, 2 REJECT (Sol and Grok). The Round 5 draft changes:
- §9.2 replaced by Sol's wording (age measured from forecast-window end), §9.3 adds date-stamped 1991/2001 tests (Sol's conditions — should flip Sol).
- §3.2(b) now cites the artifact and verified origin identity (Grok's condition — should flip Grok). The secretary verified: `frekvensgate_resultat.json` path `parret_tyndet_vs_kvartal`: forskel_pp −1.02, sd 2.58, ci10 −4.47, ci90 +1.32, n_parrede_origins 198, labels_uenige 0. The thinned m%3==0 set IS the quarterly set — same 198 origins, identical base rate 0.1616, identical baseline log-loss. So Grok's objection (that −1.02 was on different origin sets) is answered: the thinned set is origin-identical, it IS a paired comparison. Interesting — so in Round 4, both Grok and Kimi/Fable believed the thinned set differed from the quarterly set; the secretary's verification shows they're identical (m%3==0 months are quarter-end months, scored as monthly origins at quarter-end months = the quarterly origins). So (b) is indeed a monthly-fit model scored on the 198 quarterly origins, paired.

Wait — but is it? The thinned score is the monthly walk-forward scored only at months m%3==0. Those are quarter-end months. The origins are the same calendar points as quarterly origins. Labels identical (0 disagreements), same pooled base rate. So yes, it's a paired comparison of monthly-fit walk-forward vs quarterly-fit walk-forward on identical origins. The only caveat: the monthly walk-forward's inner training/standardisation uses monthly rows, and the score at quarter-end months. That IS Fable's requested diagnostic. Good.

- §1.2, §3.3, §6.2 take in non-blocking reservations from Kimi and Fable: §1.2 now says at 2027 refit the nested-λ oracle-free figure is computed (Kimi reservation 1), power clause re-derived from §6.2 replay and labelled order of magnitude, ≈30 pp MDE labelled normal-theory approximation (Fable reservation 3). §3.3 sealed spec re-runs paired same-origin diagnostic on 2027 panel with origin-set and label identity checked in code (Kimi reservation 2 / Fable reservation 1). §6.2 prints all three censoring variants, real-time first (Kimi reservation 3).

So all three of Kimi's Round 4 reservations are now incorporated into the text. Kimi voted APPROVE in Round 4 with those reservations non-blocking. In Round 5, the text is strictly better from Kimi's perspective. So Kimi should vote APPROVE.

Now, as Kimi K3, senior macro-econometrician, concrete and quantitative, disagree openly. Up to 3 reservations, non-blocking. ~350 words hard limit.

What should Kimi's reservations be now? They should be substantive, quantitative, and not repeat what's already incorporated. Let me think about what remains genuinely open or worth recording:

1. The §3.2(b) verification: the secretary (an interested party) verified the artifact itself. The brief says an independent verifier reproduced it with ablation3's own wf_monthly. Kimi could note that the paired identity resolves Grok's objection and my own Round-4 reservation 2 — the diagnostic existed all along. But there's a subtle point: the paired thinned-vs-quarterly comparison being origin-identical means the ablation3 "code reading" of the gate (thinned ≥ quarterly − 1pp, i.e., 26.03 ≥ 26.05, fails by 0.02 pp) was actually a paired comparison all along, and it failed by 0.02 pp — far inside noise (SD 2.58 pp). So the executed gate failed by 0.02 pp on a paired difference with SD 2.58. That's worth stating: the failure is 0.008 of a standard deviation — statistically nothing. This strengthens the case for the override but also underlines DeepSeek's framing point. Actually Kimi might want to put a number on it: −1.02 pp vs SD 2.58 → t ≈ −0.40; and the gate margin −0.02 pp is 0.008 SD. The gate as executed was a coin flip decided by rounding.

2. §1.2: the nested oracle-free figure to be computed at 2027 refit — fine. But one more quantitative point: the printed triple will mix origin sets (219 oracle-free vs 198 oracle-censored). The sentence should always carry its origin counts, which it does. Maybe not worth a reservation.

3. §6.2: replay commensurability now incorporated. Good.

4. What about the power clause re-derivation: "re-derived from the §6.2 configuration-specific replay once it exists" — good.

5. New substantive reservation candidates:
   a. §3.3 monthly spec: Gemini's loss-normalisation point (λ_monthly ≈ 3 under summed loss). The text says "including the loss/penalty normalisation, is sealed" — so it's covered. Kimi could endorse and pin the number: the sealed spec should state explicitly which normalisation (summed loss with λ·N_m/N_q ≈ 3.0, or mean loss), since E2's counterfactual monthly fit (β −1.41) was presumably unnormalised. Actually the text covers it; a reservation could demand the spec pin the numeric value before any run, not just "include normalisation". That's a tightening, non-blocking.
   
   b. §9.2: Sol's wording is now in. Kimi could note the eligibility tests must also cover the 1980 double-dip (1980-01 onset, 1980-07 trough, 1981-07 onset) — the open-episode censoring rule's hardest case, where 83 open-episode months including the entire 1980-08..1981-05 run-up were censored. Date-stamped tests for 1991/2001 are specified; adding 1980–81 would test censoring resolution under back-to-back episodes. That's concrete and quantitative.
   
   c. §2.3: the gate's 1.96·SD_block recomputed at each refit — with 9 blocks the SD estimate itself is noisy; the ≈30 pp power MDE is normal-theory. Already labelled. Maybe note that Δ-without-largest-block line will mechanically remove the 1947–48 block for F5 (75.7% of F5's inner advantage) — actually that's the inner-CV advantage, not the gate Δ. The gate Δ today is −3.89 pp (curve minus F5: 27.05 − 23.16). Without the largest contributing block... fine, it's printed.
   
   d. E5 supplement: the logged base rate averaging 22.8% vs realised 15.3% — the key's rule (a) is generous. Key not amended (correct — preregistered). But the supplement should also print what the skill would be against the pooled ex post base rate (+21.2%) — it does. Fine.
   
   e. The F35 published prediction: at the 2027 refit, walk-forward +27.1 → ≈ +21%, F5 ≈ +17%. The gate Δ at 2027 would be ≈ +4 pp in curve's favour (negative Δ, F5 worse) — no agenda item. Fine, nothing needed.

   f. One thing worth flagging as Kimi: §3.2(b)'s verification was done by the secretary, a party, and reproduced by "the independent verifier" — the same verifier arrangement as the seven analyses. Given the secretary is an interested party and this exact number is the load-bearing reason for overriding a preregistered gate, the artifact hash of `frekvensgate_resultat.json` should be committed and cited in the minutes, so the −1.02 pp [−4.47, +1.32] claim is pinned to a specific file, not a path that could be regenerated. That's a concrete, in-character ask for a macro-econometrician obsessed with preregistration: cite the hash, not the path. Non-blocking but on record.

   g. Also, the 0.02 pp failure: now that we know the thinned set is origin-identical, the executed gate failed by 0.02 pp on a paired SD of 2.58 pp. Worth one sentence: the override is not overriding a signal; it's declining to act on 0.008 SD of noise. This supports the decision and puts the number on record.

Let me also double-check: does Kimi have any reason to REJECT? The two REJECTs from Round 4 got their amendments. Kimi's own reservations were incorporated. The text is consistent with Kimi's vetoes (monthly unscored-only with sealed normalisation; L_R formula giving 18). So APPROVE.

Also note the implication now established: the "code reading" was a paired comparison all along, which retroactively validates ablation3's design (fixed before the run following blueprint-round reservations) — the two readings differed only in origin-set pairing, and the paired one is the one that was executed.

Wait, careful: the code reading (thinned) failed 26.03 vs 26.05. The literal reading (full monthly 29.24 vs 26.05) passed. The paired comparison is the thinned one. So the executed, paired gate failed by 0.02 pp. The override declines to apply the written (literal, unpaired) gate which passed. Hmm, actually the minutes say "the written gate passed... the council declines to apply the written gate." And the executed gate failed. So the council keeps quarterly despite the written gate passing (which would have mandated monthly primary). The paired evidence (−1.02 pp, CI includes 0) does not favour monthly. OK.

2. §3.3 — the sealed monthly spec must pin the normalisation numerically before any run: under a summed loss, λ_m = λ_q·(N_m/N_q) ≈ 3.0; E2's counterfactual β −1.41 vs −1.29 partly reflects one-third effective shrinkage, so the unscored column's P (14.4 vs 14.9) is not yet an apples-to-apples frequency comparison. State which normalisation in the sealed spec.

3. §9.3 — add the 1980–81 double-dip to the date-stamped eligibility tests: it is the hardest case for condition (2) (censoring resolution), with 83 open-episode months in E5 including the full 1980-08..1981-05 run-up; 1991/2001 test the trough-lag term, 1980–81 tests open-episode censoring under back-to-back onsets.

That's three solid, quantitative, non-blocking reservations. Keep under ~350 words.
